en: Now, let's settle this once and\nfor all.
I'm not the same as I was last\nyear, Ms. Eve! Can you still say\nthat after seeing this form!!
Ugh...! No matter what form\nyou take, I won't lose!!
Hehehe... I wonder how long\nthat bravado will last.
Now, let the battle begin...!
*Sigh*... What on earth is this\nperformance?

Apparently, it's a hanetsuki
match between Eve and Coro.
They couldn't settle it last
year, so they're determined to
do it this year...
Hanetsuki, huh... For that, Coro\nseems to be wearing some\nrather extreme gear.
Um, it's called the "Ultimate\nHanetsuki Weapon:\n<font color=yellow>Lucky-Bringing Darmizer '56</font>."

According to the instruction
manual, it has a body made of
special alloys with barriers
created by Symbol Arts, and
by linking Coro's AI to it...

I don't really get it, but I can
tell that it's definitely not
equipment meant for playing
hanetsuki,
and that Eve's physical abilities\nare completely insane for being\nable to keep up with it.
So, Captain. I take it you're the\nwitness for this duel of the\ncentury.
There's no need to use a word\nas ominous as "duel."

Getting some moderate
exercise during the New Year,
when it's easy to just eat and
sleep... isn't that a good thing?
I'll settle it right here!\nHaaaaaaaaaaaa!!
This is nothing! Try this!!
I think you're just as delusional\nfor calling this carnage\n"moderate exercise."

Still, what a lovely place. I can't
believe there's such an open
area at the peak of a mountain
range.

It's a great spot for a vacation.
I don't dislike the sea of stars,
but I still prefer to spend my
leisure time with my feet on
the ground.

Just to be safe, I've hidden the
ship with the cloaking device,
and since there are steep
mountains all around, it should
only be visible from above.

Besides, the civilization level of
this planet is roughly
equivalent to Earth's Middle
Ages, so there's no way we'll
be discovered...
Hmph, I wonder about that.
Huh?
I... I can't believe it...
Hm? Is that a local?
No way, did they actually climb\nthese steep mountains?!
Local Elder: Over here! They're\nover here! No... they are right\nhere!!

Local Woman: Oh, how divine...
You must be the party of
goddesses the <font color=yellow>Kannagi</font> spoke
of!
Wait, what is going on?!
This is bad. Coro, hide us! Now!\nAnd contact the others who\nare resting!
Y-yeeessss!!!

Local Elder: Oh! As expected
of a warrior serving the
goddesses! With a single shout,
you have exorcised that evil
presence!
Huh? No...

Local Man: Grandpa, we can
talk about that later! Come on,
everyone, stop dawdling! The
Kannagi told us!

Local Man: The beautiful
goddesses of war are
exhausted from their battle
against evil. We must hurry and
invite them to our feast to
restore their strength!
Local Residents: Yeah!!

Local Woman: Please,
Goddesses. We have prepared
palanquins for you. Please,
step inside!
Wait, what is actually going on\nhere!?
What should we do, Captain! At\nthis rate, they're really going to\ncarry us away!
Are you saying we should just\ngo along with them... Is that\nreally okay!?

Look at the desperation on
these people's faces. There
must be a reason for this. As
the Captain said, let's at least
hear them out.
Eleyna, can you see something\nwe can't?

Who knows. Come on, let's go.
Celebrating the New Year with
some local sake doesn't sound
too bad.
The priestess spoke of the\nfirst day of the Month of\nHarmony.

Upon the peaks of the
mountains in the East, three
stars descended alongside the
rising sun.
These three stars were divine\nmaidens sent to battle the evil\ndemons plaguing the land.
Drawing strength from the\nhealing feasts offered by the\npeople,
The princesses shall slay the\ndemons and restore a pure\nbreeze to this land.

First a food shortage due to
crop failure, and now a plague...
This country seems to be in
quite a state of chaos.

And then there's us, just
happening to be at the exact
spot predicted by that famous
fortune teller... the "Kannagi,"
was it?

The people here seem
absolutely convinced that
simply hosting us will be
enough to save them from
their current plight...

Situation analysis complete! It
appears the widespread crop
failure in this region is due to
climate change.	machine	gemma-4-31B-it/qat-UD-Q4_K_XL/v2+story-v1/llama.cpp-b11443/t0	2026-10-07

of malnutrition caused by the
food shortage; I found no
evidence of advanced
civilizations being involved.

So the people of this land are
facing hardships that are
simply a byproduct of natural
evolution?
That seems to be the case...

Captain, this is a difficult
decision, but intervening to
save them would be a violation
of the Uncivilized Planet
Protection Treaty.

Captain, you're saying we're
just going to find a chance to
leave... and abandon the people
of this country!!
Hey, Eve, keep your voice\ndown. They'll hear you.
But...

...That is the law of nature. If
we intervene and force an
unnatural evolution upon them,
it could lead to an even worse
situation.

All we can do is leave quietly
and pray that they overcome
this hardship through their own
strength.

Helping people in an
underdeveloped civilization
without caution could warp
their path of evolution...
Baschen might have been in a\nstate like that after Givel\nappeared...
He left everything to Givel and\nstopped thinking for himself,\nand as a result, he was used.

Local Elder: "What is the
matter, Goddesses! Such
gloomy faces will bring us bad
luck!"

Local Woman: "This meal is
humble and may not be to your
liking, but please, help
yourselves."

Was that the elder and his
granddaughter? I don't see any
food for you two; aren't you
eating?

Elder's Granddaughter: It would
be far too bold for us to share
a meal with the Goddesses...
please, do not mind us...
Is something bothering you?
Elder: Ah, no... it is but a trivial\nmatter, but...

Elder: We were told that three
Goddesses would descend. We
were simply wondering why
things are differing from the
Oracle's prophecy...
Elder's Granddaughter: Indeed,\nthe Oracle's prophecies have\nnever been wrong until now.
...Three Goddesses, huh.
What's with that look, Crowe? I\nam a perfectly fine Goddess\nmyself.

Nobleman: The old man is just
a bit of a worrywart! Please
don't let it bother you,
Goddesses! Now, let us show
you one of the finest dancers
in the land!

*Sigh*, the country is in such a
dire state, yet they're throwing
a party based on a prophecy...
I guess that's what faith is all
about.
Reimi, are you taking a break\nhere too?
Oh, Karlyn.

...I just can't help but wonder if
it's okay for the people of this
country to be doing this while
things are so bad.
Even if we pray, it's not like we\ncan actually do anything to\nhelp them...
It seems we're thinking the\nsame thing.
Warrior-like Man: Goddess, may\nI have a moment of your time?
Oh! Who are you?

Warrior-like Man: I am a
servant of the Oracle, and my
name is <font color=yellow>Yamato</font>. The Oracle
wishes to meet with the
Goddess.
The Oracle... the one who\nprophesied our arrival.
Finally arrived, have you?
Yamato: Hm? And who might\nyou be?
Things will go much smoother if\nI'm present for the discussion\nwith this Oracle. I'll come along.
Eleyna, what do you mean? If\nyou know something...
The Oracle will explain the\nsituation. Now, let's go.
Yamato: Very well. Please,\nfollow me.
Yamato: This way, please.\nPlease watch your step, as it is\nquite dark.
What is this place? I can't\nbelieve there was something\nlike this beyond the cave...!
I wonder if the writing on the\nwalls is the language of the\npeople of this land?

Please, do not touch them.
Your powerful energy might
weaken the power of the
"Oracle."

It is an honor to meet you. I am
the one who serves as the
shrine maiden of this land, my
name is <font color=yellow>Iyo</font>.

Iyo: I sincerely apologize for
involving visitors from the Sea
of Stars in the affairs of our
country.
What, the Sea of Stars!? Just\nhow much do you know about\nus!?

Iyo: I am aware that you are
foreigners who possess an ark
that traverses the Sea of
Stars and have come to this
land to rest.
How could you possibly...

Did you not hear this person
mention the "Oracle" just now?
Like me, they possess the
power to see through all of the
past and future.

Iyo: Unfortunately, I am merely
a descendant of such a
person. I do not possess the
power to hear the oracles
myself.

Iyo: All I can do is decipher the
records of the future left upon
these walls by the first shrine
maiden.

So you saw that and... no, you
mean you've known about
us―about this universe―for a
long time?
Iyo: Yes, that is correct.

Iyo: However, if the people of
this land were to suddenly
learn of this, chaos would be
inevitable. That is why no one
is permitted to enter this
shrine except for the Oracle
and their guardians.
I believe we have the gist of it.\nWhy don't we get to the point?
Iyo: Thank you.

Iyo: I wish to eradicate the
faith in the Oracle in this land
and incite a rebellion among
the people.

What?! What do you mean?
The country is already in
chaos, right? You want to start
a rebellion on top of that?!

Iyo: Precisely why. Now is the
only time a rebellion is possible,
while the country is in turmoil
and the people's frustrations
are peaking.
...I don't understand. Iyo, what\nexactly are you trying to do?

Iyo: According to the Oracle's
records written here, this
nation will fall in 278 days. It is
written that in the ensuing
chaos, 90% of the population
will perish.

90% of the people?! If that
happens, it's only a matter of
time before the survivors die
too...
Iyo: Yes. That is why I wish to\noverturn this prophecy.

An oracle is but one possible
future. However, overturning it
requires more than ordinary
strength.
Ichiyo: Yes, which is why I must\ncast aside faith and incite a\npopular uprising.
So that's what was happening\nwhile those three disappeared\nduring yesterday's banquet.
Still, that priestess has some\nserious guts.

Holding a massive feast under
her own orders while the
people are starving from poor
harvests, just to draw all the
resentment toward herself.

Then, she'll show the people us
being defeated by the demons
to drive home the fact that the
prophecy was wrong... huh.

True, if the people are this
blindly devoted to the
priestess, the shock of a failed
prophecy would be immense.

Furthermore, it seems the core
members of the rebel army
have already been arranged
under Yamato's direction.

The plan is to have the elite
force Yamato gathered defeat
the demons, turning them into
heroes.

Thorough as always. I guess
the idea is that if there are
heroes to lead the country
next, the chaos following the
rebellion will be kept to a
minimum.

What was written in that shrine
was likely the future that
awaits a people who cling to
oracles and can do nothing but
pray to the gods.

If a great shift occurs in the
people's consciousness, it may
be possible to overturn the
oracle.

But what happens to Iyo? The
plan is to make everyone
resent her as the priestess to
spark a rebellion, right? I can't
imagine she'll get out of this
unscathed.

It seems they've already made
preparations for her to flee to
another country, making it look
like Yamato defeated her when
the rebellion breaks out.

This is an internal matter for
this country, and getting
involved recklessly could
potentially violate the
Uncharted Planet Protection
Treaty.
But I still want to help Iyo.

I believe this is a fight for the
people of this land to break
free from the supernatural
power of the oracle and return
to the path of proper evolution.
So, Captain, everyone, please...

I agree with the Captain. I'll
help even if you don't ask. I
can't just abandon lives right in
front of me.
So, what about our "demon"\nwho's always nagging us about\nprotecting uncharted planets?
Of course! If the Captain says\nit's okay, I'm all in! No problem\nat all!

I can use 'Darmizer'56,' whom
everyone in the country
believes to be the incarnation
of evil,

to make it look like I crushed
Eve and the others, or to act
as if I was defeated by Yamato
and his group. It'll be a piece of
cake!
Though I'm not thrilled about\nthe idea of being defeated by\nCoro.
I heard Iyo's words of resolve\nwith my own ears. I have no\nreason to object.

It has been since you stopped
the resurrection of Asmodeus
that I last saw an oracle
overturned. I look forward to it.
Reimi, we are all of one mind.\nWe will fight to seize the\nrightful future of this country!
Thank you, everyone!
Now, let us settle this. In the\nname of the gods, I cannot\noverlook any further folly!
Now, let us fight with honor...!

(Wait, what's wrong, Coro! Did
you forget your lines!?
Everyone is watching, get it
together!!)
(Ugh, hey!! This isn't what we\ndiscussed!)
(Karlyn! Everyone is watching!\nFor now, let's just keep\nfighting!!)
Gah!!
Karlyn, are you okay!? Coro,\nwait! You've gone way too far!!
Everyone!! This is an\nemergency!! Please evacuate\nimmediately!!
Finally, the comms are working!\nListen, you need to learn some\nrestraint...!!
That's not it, Eve! That's not\nme! It's moving on its own\nwithout being linked to my AI!!
What? That outer shell is\nmoving by itself!?

It seems so. I'm searching for
the cause now, but there's a
special barrier preventing me
from accessing the control
mechanism...
Can you see something,\nEleyna!?
No, I can't tell...
(But for even me to be unable\nto read it...)
She's right, Captain! Let's\nprioritize the evacuation of the\ncitizens first!

We'll secure the retreat.
Yamato, take your unit and
protect everyone gathered
here and get them to safety!
Yamato: I cannot retreat.

Don't be stubborn! We don't
even understand the situation
ourselves! First, you all need to
get to a safe place...

Yamato: If we retreat under
your protection, my people will
never be able to break free
from their faith in the gods and
the miko!
But with your equipment, trying\nto fight that weapon is...
Yamato: Nevertheless, this is a\nbattle for our very future!
Yamato: Everyone, follow me!!
Dammit...! We can't just leave it\nto them! Captain, let's fight!
Elite Warrior: Hyaaaaah!

The enemy flinched! As
expected of an elite unit. Their
training and morale are higher
than I imagined.

But with so few of us, we can
only hold out for so long!
Captain, I'll go command the
evacuation in the rear.
Elite Warrior: Guh... is this... the\nend...?

Yamato: Stand up! Do not
falter!! Raise your heads and
stare down the enemy! Our
future lies only there!
...!! Damn it... I can't let us lose\nhere...! Raaaaaaagh!!
Everyone, hurry down the\nmountain! I'll lead the way, so\nplease follow my instructions!

...Why? Why are those people
fighting? The Priestess's
prophecy said the Goddess
would slay the demons for us.

If we just follow the Priestess
without question, everything
will work out... Why are those
people doing this...!?
Elder, do you honestly believe\nthis situation will resolve itself\nif you do nothing?
...G-Goddess. I... I...

Regardless, it's dangerous
here! Prioritize the wounded
and the children during the
evacuation!
Goddess! I'll go gather\neveryone who can use healing\narts!
Please do!
You! What on earth are you\ndoing?!

I'm going to lend Yamato a
hand! With the crops failing,
I've barely used a hoe lately―I
was starting to feel like I was
getting rusty!

I appreciate it, but know when
to retreat! Please, don't let
your courage turn into
recklessness!

Elder: What are you thinking!
Do you not believe in the
Goddess's victory!? Do you
dare doubt the Miko's
prophecy!?

Elder, this isn't a matter of
belief. When your comrades are
fighting right in front of you,
it's only natural to lend a hand.
Now, I will go and guide\neveryone to safety.
Youth: I'm going too! Gramps,\nyou go help the Goddess!\nEveryone will listen to you.
What, reinforcements!?\nYamato, were you still\npreparing troops?

Yamato: N-no... But those
faces... they're military officers
and officials from the Central
Council... What on earth is
happening?
There are dozens of times\nmore people here than an elite\nsquad. At this rate...!
Yes, let's settle this in one go!
Did it stop...?

I've gained access to
Darmizer'56's control
mechanism! It won't go on
rampaging now!
Yamato: We did it... We actually\npulled it off...
Yamato: WE WONNNNN!!!!
Thank goodness. For a moment\nthere, I wasn't sure how things\nwould turn out...

Thanks to everyone's
cooperation, it looks like no
one suffered any serious
injuries. Thank you all so much!
Elder's Granddaughter: Oh, to\nreceive such words from the\nGoddess... I am humbled.

Young Man: If anything, we
were only able to fight because
of the Goddess!! Seeing her
bravery boosts our morale! A
true Goddess of War!
I'm sorry for deceiving you all\nuntil now. We aren't gods or\nanything like that...
We are humans, just like you.
Young Man: Huh...?

We were born in a place far
from here, and our ancestors
faced and overcame disasters
many times, just like the ones
you are facing now.

So, we are just humans who
happen to know a few more
tricks and a bit more wisdom
for survival than you do.

In fact, I lived deep
underground because the
surface had become a polluted
wasteland where people could
no longer survive.
Yamato: ...C-could such a thing\nactually happen?
Unfortunately, yes.

But that was the result of my
parents and many others
thinking desperately to pass a
glimmer of hope on to the
future.

There are depths of despair
that make you want to cling to
a god. ...But that should only
happen after you've done your
absolute best.
The gods don't smile upon\nthose who do nothing.

Ichiyo: The cause of the faith
that led our people to cling to
the gods lies with us, the clan
of the Miko.
Elder: Lady Ichiyo! You were\nhere!? What is the meaning of\nthis...!

Ichiyo: First, to the travelers
from afar, and to everyone
gathered here: I thank you
from the bottom of my heart
for saving our nation from its
plight.
Ichiyo: And now... please, listen.
...!! Ichiyo, you aren't planning to\ntalk about the prophecy here,\nare you!?
Yamato: Lady Iyo! You mustn't!!
Iyo: Yamato, stand back. I will\ntell them everything... including\nthe sins of our shrine maidens.

Elder: ...M-My Lady. Then what
were the prophecies all this
time...? I thought you were
always guiding us on the
righteous path...!!

Iyo: By reading the prophecies
left by the first shrine maiden,
one can predict the future to a
certain extent.

Iyo: However, since the
descriptions are not detailed,
some shrine maidens have
passed them off as prophecies
to lead the people. I am no
exception.
Elder: ...How can this be! Are\nyou saying you shrine maidens\nhave been deceiving us?!
I don't think that's right.

I got a look inside the shrine,
and there were piles of
documents―domestic affairs,
annual crop yields, the
movements of neighboring
countries, new technologies...

I believe the successive shrine
maidens used those documents
to seek the best possible path,
and then guided the country
by presenting those findings as
prophecies.
They bore that heavy burden\nalone, unable to tell anyone...

Elder's Granddaughter: We just
wanted to take the easy way
out by leaving everything to
the shrine maiden...

Young Man: I'm sorry. We didn't
know any of that; we just
thought we should put all our
faith in the shrine maiden...
It is not all your fault.
Elder: Hmm?

The successive priestesses
underestimated the strength of
the people. They were so
desperate to handle everything
themselves that they refused
to rely on anyone. Iyo, you are
the same, aren't you?

Have you seen the people of
this land fight with Dauntless
Courage? They are far more
reliable than you think.

Iyo: ...You are right. It seems it
was my own way of thinking,
rather than the country, that
needed to change.

Youth: Then please, count on
us from now on, Priestess! If
we all work together, I'm sure
we can do something about the
poor harvests and the plague!
Iyo: ...But, the clan of\npriestesses has continued to\ndeceive you all for decades...!

Elder's Granddaughter: ...It
must have been painful to lie
just to protect us. From now
on, we won't just rely on you;
we will walk beside you.
Iyo, there is no one here who\nwants to condemn you.

Besides, you've gone through
all those piles of documents,
right? Your knowledge is
necessary for the future of
this country.

Elder: ...I haven't lived this long
for nothing. I have some
knowledge of farming methods.
I shall call upon the other
elders as well.
Iyo: Elder...! Thank you so much.

I suppose this is exactly what
they call a new beginning for
this country. It's a perfect fit
for this scenery!

This story has come to an end.
More stories are planned for
release in the future. Please
look forward to them.

Yamato: The issues with food
and plague won't be resolved
overnight, but meetings to find
a solution are progressing. It is
all thanks to everyone.

No, it was the hard work of the
elite squad that moved
people's hearts. We didn't
really...
You looked the part, leading\nthat elite squad, Yamato.
Yamato: In that case, I am\neven more grateful to the two\nof you.

Yamato: If it weren't for Reimi's
words back then, I think I would
still be agonizing over it and
would never have been able to
lead the squad like that...
The day before the final battle

Yamato, this elite squad you
summoned is quite a force.
They're disciplined and their
morale is high. Are they your
subordinates?
Yamato: No, they are comrades\nfrom when I was assigned to\nguard the northern border.

I heard from Iyo that this
country is under invasion from
a neighboring nation. That's
why everyone is so
accustomed to combat, isn't
it?

Yamato: Yes. Furthermore,
everyone is risking everything
on the hope that this battle will
change this country.
Risking everything?

Yamato: The border regions
originally received little aid
from the capital and were poor,
but this recent crop failure has
pushed them into the worst
possible situation.

Yamato: If this war changes
the country, there is a chance
they can save their families
who suffer from disease and
hunger. That is why morale is
so high.
Yamato, what about you?
Yamato: Me...?
...It's a lie, isn't it? That there's\na country willing to shelter Iyo\nif a rebellion breaks out.
Yamato: ...!!

She intends to end this
rebellion through her own
execution to build a new
nation.

Yamato: ...My apologies. The
Miko forbade me from speaking
of it, fearing it would worry you
all.

Yamato, are you really okay
with this? A reform built upon
the sacrifice of someone who
loves her country that much!
Yamato: ...It is not a matter of\nwhether I am okay with it or\nnot...

Yamato: The Miko has decided.
As her guardian, I will carry out
my duty with every ounce of
my strength until the end.
I can tell just by watching you\ndraw your bow. I can see the\nhesitation in your heart...

Even if this is all a play, you're
the one leading the troops into
battle. If the commander is in
that state, won't it cause
problems for everyone?
If there is something going on,\ncould you please tell us about\nit?
Yamato: ...You are truly honest\npeople. It seems I cannot\ndeceive you.

Yamato: ...The truth is, there
was once a time when I tried
to kidnap the Miko and run
away.
That was about ten years ago,\nwhen the Miko was still in her\nteens.
The country was in chaos, with\ncrop failures continuing across\nthe land, just as they are now.
She must have been working\nwithout sleep or rest,\nsearching for a solution,
for the Miko looked terrible.\nDesperate to get her to drink\nsome medicinal tea,
I broke the taboo and stepped\ninside the Miko's shrine.
And there, I discovered what\nlay within the shrine―the truth\nabout the Miko...

I repeatedly urged her to make
it public, believing it was not a
responsibility a teenage girl
should have to bear, but she
never agreed.
Then, the incident occurred.

Driven to desperation by the
food shortage that showed no
sign of improving, young people
from the frontier stormed the
Central Council.
Fires broke out all across the\ntown.
As I protected her and fled\nthrough the chaos, I realized\nthat this was an opportunity.
Taking advantage of the\nconfusion, I stole a horse and\nled her away.

I told her, "Let us abandon a
country that burdens you with
such a heavy responsibility,
and live our lives together."
As we rode, we spoke of what\nshe wished to do once we had\nleft the country...
Yamato: While I was resting the\nhorse, she had vanished.
So Iyo had already resolved\nher path in life, even at that\nage.
Yamato: From that moment on,\nI decided to align myself with\nher resolve.

Yamato: I am the blade that
carries out her wishes. Until
the moment she desires death,
I shall grant it.
And you're just going to leave\neverything up to Iyo-san like\nthat?

If you just give up because you
can't change her mind and
stop thinking for yourself,
aren't you just like everyone
else in the country?
Yamato: ...!!
...Yamato. Could you tell me\nwhat you're really thinking?
Yamato: ...I...

Yamato: ...I want to protect
Lady Iyo...!! But if I do, this
country she loves so dearly
will...!
Then it's settled. Let's protect\nthem both. Lady Iyo and this\ncountry!

Even if people call it reckless,
as long as you have an
unwavering resolve within you,
a way will open. I'll help you!

Yamato: To think that I, too,
had become someone who
would place such a heavy
burden on the Miko... I am truly
ashamed.

I'm sure there's a way to
protect both the future of this
country and Lady Iyo. As long
as we don't forget to search
